abstract.p: There has been much recent work in the shuffle model of differential privacy, particularly for approximate d-bin histograms. While these protocols achieve low error, the number of messages sent by each user-the message complexity-has so far scaled with d or the privacy parameters. The message complexity is an informative predictor of a shuffle protocol's resource consumption. We present a protocol whose message complexity is two when there are sufficiently many users. The protocol essentially pairs each row in the dataset with a fake row and performs a simple randomization on all rows. We show that the error introduced by the protocol is small, using rigorous analysis as well as experiments on real-world data. We also prove that corrupt users have a relatively low impact on our protocol's estimates.
